core.title: Construct collaborators only in a composition root
core.given: A source file assigned to a layer role by the stack's role assignment, and not a composition root (roots are identified by the stack's role map)
core.when: it constructs a collaborator (the construction construct and the collaborator name patterns come from the stack's profile)
core.then: Construct the collaborator only in a composition root.
prefer: Construct in a composition root; the stack's application assembly point counts as a root when it is where the application, its boundary and their dependencies are wired.
Pass the constructed collaborator from the root to the consumer that needs it.
During GREEN: add only the wiring the current behavior requires.
During GREEN: reuse existing factories, instances and composition patterns before creating new ones.
During GREEN: keep construction separate from application or presentation behavior.
avoid: Instantiating the collaborator in the consumer as a shortcut.
Centralizing unrelated wiring merely because the root is being edited.
unless: Test files and the stack's never-scanned (vendored/build) trees.
Files assigned to no layer role: outside these rules, not in violation.
core.why: Scattered wiring is not a style problem: it is why a test cannot substitute anything, and why a second deployment shape becomes a rewrite.
evidence: The current behavioral acceptance passes through the real wiring.
Collaborator construction remains confined to a composition root: the stack's convention check reports no collaborator construction outside a root.
verification: The check is a content-level scan of current source (not a diff) for collaborator construction (per the stack's construction idiom and collaborator naming) in any scanned file that is not a composition root; all such constructions present count, not only newly added ones.

Which files count as scanned source is owned by the stack's own source classification (its repository topology and source kinds), not by any extension or file-name restriction of this rule; the scan covers every file the stack classifies as source.
Scan lexically masked source so occurrences inside string literals or comments are not flagged.

Never scan test files: test-file classification is owned by the stack's repository topology, not by this rule. Never scan the stack's excluded trees; roots.excluded is one stack-wide list and the exact exclusion classification is owned by the stack's checker.
Files assigned to no layer role are out of scope, not in violation.
External-package imports (recognised per the stack's external-import idiom) resolve outside the project graph and are not layer-checked.

values: collaborator constructed outside a composition root (scan of current source, string- and comment-masked)

fires: An application or boundary module constructs a collaborator to obtain its dependency, whether the construction is new or pre-existing.
A presentation module constructs an outbound collaborator (such as a client or gateway) inline instead of receiving it.
A module that is not a composition root constructs a factory or provider to build its own collaborators.
doesNotFire: The construction is in a composition root (per the stack's role map).
The construction is in a test file or an excluded (vendored/build) tree.
The file is assigned to no layer role.
The construction appears only inside a string literal or comment.
The constructed name does not match the stack's collaborator designation.

bunOnly.text: `server.ts` counts as a root because `Bun.serve` is the full-stack app's assembly point, where routes and their dependencies are wired.
bunOnly.reason: The runtime's server entry and its assembly-point rationale are stack-specific; the core says only that the stack's designated assembly point counts, and the profile lists which artifact kinds are composition roots.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself (construct collaborators only in a composition root, pass them to consumers) is fully neutral. What could not be made neutral: (1) the Bun.serve assembly-point rationale for why the server entry is a root (bunOnly; the profile records the artifact kind), (2) the concrete construction construct `new <Name>()`, the collaborator name suffixes and the root basenames (profile values via two proposed idiom keys plus roles.composition_root.path), and (3) the detector and finding ids (bunOnly, per the notProfileKeys rule). The Bun rule imposes no file-extension restriction of its own: which files count as scanned source, which are test files, and the exact vendored/build exclusion are all owned by the stack's repository topology and its checker, so they are stated in core verification rather than as profile values (suffix.source is a filename-pattern list and roots.excluded holds only the stack-wide never-scanned tree list). String- and comment-masking was kept as generic lexical masking since string literals and comments are near-universal lexical categories; severity 3 / strict disposition is carried in core verification, not the profile.
